what: Kaspi.kz runs the dominant digital platform in Kazakhstan. Its app combines payments, a marketplace for goods and services, and consumer lending, used by most adults in the country, and it has expanded into Turkey.
customers: Kazakh consumers and merchants, and increasingly Turkish users through the acquired Hepsiburada marketplace.
money: transaction fees on card and app payments
commissions on goods and services sold through the app
moat: A single app that most Kazakhs use daily for payments, shopping and borrowing, which gives it transaction data no bank or retailer in the country can match.
risks: It depends almost entirely on one small country's economy
Kazakh regulatory or political change could affect it quickly
Turkish expansion is a large and unfamiliar market
Consumer lending losses would rise in a downturn
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 69% and an operating margin of 53%, exceptional figures
Revenue grew about 60% last year and about 47% a year over three years
A dividend yield above 6% alongside that growth
watch: Kazakh transaction volumes and the Turkish expansion's losses.
